# Comprehensive Requirements Quality Checklist: Workflow Domain Management

**Purpose**: Validate requirement completeness, clarity, testability, and architectural compliance for the Workflow Domain before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-11-04
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | **Plan**: [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## 1. State Machine & Lifecycle Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all valid state transitions explicitly defined with unambiguous source and target state pairs in the specification?
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec clearly prohibit transitions from terminal states (`Completed`, `Cancelled`) without exception?
- [ ] CHK003 Is the cancellation boundary strictly defined such that `Approved` or `Completed` Work Items cannot transition to `Cancelled`?
- [ ] CHK004 Does the specification define expected error codes and error payloads when an illegal state jump is requested?
- [ ] CHK005 Are concurrent transition race conditions (e.g., simultaneous reviewer actions) addressed with explicit locking/conflict resolution requirements?

## 2. Batching & Work Distribution (Assignment)

- [ ] CHK006 Is the relationship between a `WorkItem` and batched assets (`resource_type = "ANNOTATION_BATCH"`) specified with child item tracking expectations?
- [ ] CHK007 Does the spec define behavior when a dataset size is not evenly divisible by the requested batch size?
- [ ] CHK008 Are bulk distribution requirements (round-robin vs quota-based) unambiguously stated for multiple annotators?
- [ ] CHK009 Does the specification define what happens when a Work Item is reassigned while in `InProgress` or `Assigned` status?
- [ ] CHK010 Is primary user ownership (`assignee_id`) differentiated clearly from team/role metadata?

## 3. Review Feedback & Audit Trail Integrity

- [ ] CHK011 Is the review feedback comment explicitly specified as optional for both `Approved` and `Rejected` transitions?
- [ ] CHK012 Does the spec require immutable append-only persistence for every state change in `workflow_history`?
- [ ] CHK013 Are all required audit log attributes (`from_state`, `to_state`, `changed_by`, `comment`, `changed_at`) defined with strict typing?
- [ ] CHK014 Is the query specification for retrieving chronological Work Item history testable and clear?

## 4. Clean Architecture & DDD Compliance

- [ ] CHK015 Are domain entities (`WorkflowDefinitionEntity`, `WorkItemEntity`, `AssignmentEntity`, `WorkflowHistoryEntity`) specified as pure Python with zero ORM or framework imports?
- [ ] CHK016 Are all repository and engine dependencies in use cases abstracted via `typing.Protocol` interfaces?
- [ ] CHK017 Is `user_id` (`assignee_id`, `assigned_by`, `changed_by`) strictly enforced as an integer across all contract boundaries?
- [ ] CHK018 Are use cases cleanly decoupled into single-responsibility modules under `application/use_cases/`?

## 5. Non-Functional & Boundary Validation

- [ ] CHK019 Is the performance threshold (<150ms p95 for state transitions) testable with defined synthetic workload conditions?
- [ ] CHK020 Are notification services explicitly documented as out-of-scope for v1 to prevent scope creep?
- [ ] CHK021 Is behavior defined when the underlying referenced asset/batch is deleted from the storage/dataset domain?

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- Items are numbered sequentially (CHK001–CHK021) for unambiguous reference in code reviews and discussions
